_README: Episode backlog for the podcast studio. episode-draft.mjs --auto picks the first case here that has no draft and no published episode yet (matched by slug). Every case is well documented in public court records and major-outlet reporting, so the script can stay factual without inventing detail. Keep entries evergreen. Add a case any time; the studio reads this file live.

cases.title: The Golden State Killer
cases.angle: How forensic genealogy ended a forty-year hunt for Joseph DeAngelo, and what the 2020 plea hearing put on the record.

cases.title: Gabby Petito
cases.angle: The van-life timeline, the Moab traffic stop body-cam footage, and how the case reshaped how police handle domestic calls.

cases.title: The Gilgo Beach Murders
cases.angle: A decade of remains along Ocean Parkway, the 2023 arrest of Rex Heuermann, and where the charges stand.

cases.title: Chris Watts: The Interrogation
cases.angle: What the released interview footage and the discovery documents show about how the confession unfolded.

cases.title: Elisa Lam and the Cecil Hotel
cases.angle: The elevator footage, what the coroner actually concluded, and how the internet built a case that was never there.

cases.title: Alex Murdaugh
cases.angle: The kennel video timestamp, the financial crimes underneath the murders, and the 2023 verdict.

cases.title: BTK: The Floppy Disk
cases.angle: How a metadata slip on a church computer ended thirty years of letters from Dennis Rader.

cases.title: The Zodiac Killer
cases.angle: The confirmed attacks, the ciphers that were solved and the ones that were not, and why the case is still open.

cases.title: Lori Vallow Daybell
cases.angle: The missing-children timeline in Rexburg, the doomsday beliefs entered into evidence, and the 2023 conviction.

cases.title: Maura Murray
cases.angle: A crashed car on Route 112 in New Hampshire, a disappearance in under ten minutes, and twenty years of no answers.

cases.title: Scott Peterson
cases.angle: The Christmas Eve disappearance of Laci Peterson, the Berkeley Marina, and what the LA Innocence Project is now arguing.

cases.title: Ted Bundy: The Two Escapes
cases.angle: The courthouse window in Aspen, the ceiling in Glenwood Springs, and the Florida murders that followed.

cases.title: JonBenet Ramsey: The DNA
cases.angle: What the touch DNA tested in 2008 did and did not prove, and why Boulder reopened testing in 2023.

cases.title: Adnan Syed
cases.angle: The Hae Min Lee case, the cell tower evidence, the 2022 release and the 2023 reinstated conviction.

cases.title: Amanda Knox
cases.angle: The Meredith Kercher case in Perugia, two convictions, two acquittals, and the 2015 final ruling.

cases.title: Bryan Kohberger: The Case File
cases.angle: The knife sheath DNA, the white Elantra, and the plea that closed the Idaho student murders case.

cases.title: Delphi: The Bridge Guy
cases.angle: The Snapchat video, the unspent round, and the 2024 conviction of Richard Allen for the murders of Abby Williams and Libby German.

cases.title: Casey Anthony
cases.angle: Thirty-one days, the chloroform searches, and why the jury acquitted in 2011.

cases.title: Steven Avery
cases.angle: Eighteen years for a rape he did not commit, then the Teresa Halbach murder conviction that Making a Murderer put on trial.

cases.title: Madeleine McCann
cases.angle: The Praia da Luz apartment, the timeline of the checks, and the 2020 German suspect.

cases.title: The Tylenol Murders
cases.angle: Seven deaths in Chicago in 1982, the case that invented tamper-proof packaging, and why nobody has been convicted.

cases.title: The McStay Family
cases.angle: A family gone from Fallbrook, graves in the Mojave three years later, and the business partner convicted in 2019.

cases.title: The Laundrie Notebook
cases.angle: What the FBI released about the notebook found in the Carlton Reserve and how it closed the Petito case.

cases.title: Kendrick Johnson
cases.angle: The gym mat in Valdosta, two autopsies with different findings, and the case that was reopened and closed again.

cases.title: Delphi: The Appeal
cases.angle: A follow-up to the 2022 episode, for listeners who already know the case. Spend ONE short chapter recapping February 13 2017, the Monon High Bridge, Abby Williams, Libby German and the phone recording. Everything after that is what has happened SINCE: the October 2022 arrest of Richard Allen, the 2024 trial, the prison statements the defence attributed to psychosis, the November 2024 conviction, the 130-year sentence, and the appeal argued before the Indiana Court of Appeals on September 21 2026. He is convicted and appealing; say so, and do not treat the appeal as proof either way.

cases.title: Murders in Moscow: The Plea
cases.angle: DO NOT RETELL THE MURDERS. This is a follow-up for listeners who already heard the 2025 episode. Chapter 1 and ONLY chapter 1 recaps November 13 2022 in a few sentences: the King Road house, Ethan Chapin, Madison Mogen, Xana Kernodle, Kaylee Goncalves, the two surviving roommates, the knife-sheath DNA, the arrest. Chapters 2 through 12 cover ONLY what happened after the arrest and must not revisit the night of the murders: the capital case and the death-penalty filing, the defence motions and the DNA and cell-site fights, the June 30 2025 plea agreement, the July 2 2025 guilty plea to all five counts with appeals waived, the victim impact statements, the July 23 2025 sentencing to four consecutive life terms plus ten years, the gag order and released case files, and the July 2026 motion to withdraw the plea claiming ineffective counsel and coercion. He pleaded guilty and is serving life; he has moved to withdraw that plea and the court has not ruled.

cases.title: Erik and Lyle: The Parole Years
cases.angle: A follow-up to the 2024 episode, for listeners who already know the case. ONE short chapter recapping August 20 1989, the killings of Jose and Kitty Menendez, the two trials and the 1996 conviction and life-without-parole sentence. The rest is what has happened since: the habeas petition and the new evidence claims, the May 2025 resentencing to 50 years to life that made them parole eligible, the August 2025 parole hearings that denied both brothers for three years, and the board's September 2026 decision to advance the next hearing to March 2027.

cases.title: JonBenet Ramsey: Thirty Years
cases.angle: A follow-up to the 2022 episodes, timed to the thirtieth anniversary in December 2026. ONE short chapter recapping December 26 1996, the ransom note, the 5:52 a.m. call and the discovery in the basement. The rest is the thirty years since and what has moved recently: the 2008 touch-DNA testing and the exoneration letter, the grand jury documents, Boulder Police's annual updates, and the department's December 2025 statement that it had conducted new interviews and re-tested evidence with current DNA technology. Nobody has ever been charged; name no suspects.
